title: Customer Support CRM Search Out-of-Order Response Overwrite
businessContext: In a high-volume customer support ticketing portal, agents type customer email addresses into a live autocomplete bar. Often, typing "alexander" shows search results for "alex" because the earlier network request for "alex" took 600ms while the later request for "alexander" took 150ms.
problemStatement: Because network latency varies unpredictably, asynchronous responses return out-of-order. The component currently sets state whenever any promise resolves. Implement request cancellation using `AbortController` and ignore stale in-flight results.
constraints: When user types, earlier in-flight requests must be aborted or their results discarded.
Debounce input to prevent API flood (e.g. 250ms).
Properly handle AbortError without triggering uncaught exception logs.
candidateTasks: Identify how variable network latency produces stale state overwrites.
Catch `err.name === "AbortError"` gracefully so aborted requests do not set error state.
hints: Return a cleanup function from `useEffect`: `return () => controller.abort()`.

testCases.name: Discards stale in-flight responses and aborts signal
testCases.explanation: Cleanly cancels superseded fetch requests on dependency change.

alternativeApproaches: Using TanStack Query (React Query) or SWR with automatic request deduplication and query cancellation.
Using a request sequence ID ref (e.g. currentSeqRef.current === seq) to ignore outdated responses.
commonMistakes: Only using a boolean flag "let active = true; ... return () => active = false": this ignores state update but does not abort the network request, consuming client bandwidth and battery.
Failing to catch AbortError, resulting in noisy unhandled promise rejection warnings in the browser console.
